summary: The two edits carry the same content and cover the intent. Both put the routing dynamic import on routing-forms, but the import happens in the calendar sync code. Both also split the owner/email/event-type check across the two edges and repeat the cancellation flag and the precondition checks.

findings.detail: "Use the requested dynamic import for routing dependencies to keep webhook module initialization from loading the problematic UI dependency chain" is about how CalendarSyncService (calendar-subscription, which owns packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/sync/CalendarSyncService.ts) imports those dependencies. Routing-forms itself does not change, so this belongs on calendar-subscription, next to the booking-service dynamic import.

"Only invoke it once the required owner and email information is present" (cancel edge) and "Only invoke it once the required event-type information is present" (reschedule edge) split the check across the two services. The intent says only "Check required owner, email, and event-type information before invoking those services", without saying which field gates which service.

"with `skipCalendarSyncTaskCancellation` so Cal.com updates its booking without trying to delete the external event again" appears almost word for word on both the cancel-booking/handle-cancel-booking node and the e-sync-cancel-booking edge.

The precondition check is stated on calendar-subscription ("Check required owner, email, and event-type information before invoking the booking services") and again on both edges ("Only invoke it once the required ... information is present").
